title.narrative: ADB Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility
ADB Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility

description.narrative: CEFs huvudsakliga mål är att finansiera projekt inom "ren Energi", dvs. förnybart, energieff, och tillgång till energi. Fonden finansierar även pilotprojekt, utveckling av policy, finansieringsmetoder etc. för att stimulere ren energi.

Clean Energy Fund is part of ADB Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility. Main objective to finance projects in clean energy, major demonstration projects, policy development and mode of fundings.

The Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility (CEFPF) was established in 2007 to help improve energy security in Developing Member Countries (DMCs) and decrease the rate of climate change. It will do this by financing the deployment of new, more efficient and less polluting supply and end-use technologies, through either grant or non-grant resources. The CEFPF is composed of the Clean Energy Fund (CEF), the Asian Clean Energy Fund (ACEF), the Carbon Capture and Storage Fund (CCSF) and the Canadian Climate Fund for the Private Sector in Asia (CFPS).

sector.narrative: Energy generation, renewable sources - multiple technologies

description.narrative:
The Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility (CEFPF) has continued to support the clean energy transition in the Asian Development Bank's (ADB) developing member countries (DMCs) through financing, technical assistance, and knowledge-sharing activities. The following are summarizes the key results achieved from the 2024 CEFPF Annual Report.
Progress Toward Clean Energy Targets based on the annual report 2024:
- CEFPF-supported projects in 2024 contributed to an additional 76.1 MW of renewable energy capacity, bringing the cumulative total to 3,601 MW, which surpassed the 2025 target.
- CEFPF monitors emissions reductions achieved through the increased use of renewable energy and emissions avoided through energy efficiency measures. Supported projects in 2024 are expected to result to 2.7 million tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e)/year emission reduction, contributing to the estimated total emission reduction of 32.7 million tCO2e/year. This is approaching the target of 35 million tCO2e/year by 2025 in accordance with the current Design Monitoring Framework (DMF), but it will not be fully achieved by 2025. The DMF is expected to be revised upon the available funding.
- The CEFPF supports projects that enable DMCs to implement measures that improve energy efficiency. To date, CEFPF has supported projects that will conserve 12.6 terawatt-hour equivalent (TWh-eq) of energy per year, though still short of the 21 TWh target.
Scaling Clean Energy Investments:
- ADB investments leveraged by CEFPF reached $6.2 billion, exceeding the cumulative target.
- The fund maintained a strong leverage ratio where every $1 of CEFPF financing attracted $26 of clean energy investment from other sources.
Technology Deployment and Innovation:
- 56 clean energy technologies have been deployed in 37 countries. In 2024 alone, 7 new technologies were introduced, including smart grid systems, renewable heating, and digital decarbonization tools.
- CEFPF supported new business models and pilot projects, like distributed solar for public infrastructure in Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Maldives, and Sri Lanka.
Policy and Capacity Building:
- At output level on "barriers to clean energy and/or CCS investment lowered", 25 national or local policies enabling clean energy and/or CCS development in participating DMCs developed by 2025. For example, In the first half of 2025, the CEFPF supported the TA Supporting Affordable and Sustainable Energy Transition, which aims to provide policy advice and develop capacity to support Indonesias transition to clean energy. The TA will also contribute to the design and implementation of policy actions for the subprograms of the ADB policy-based loan (PBL) of the same project name, Affordable and Sustainable Energy Transition.
- The CEFPF continues to build institutional capacity through trainings, workshops, and conferences, including support for the 2025 Asia Clean Energy Forum held at ADB headquarters. To date, it has supported 672 capacity-building events with 28,033 participants, including 5,959 women. As womens participation remains quite low, the Embassy will encourage CEFPF to increase this target.
Gender and Social Inclusion:
-To date, 85% of CEFPF projects are categorized either Gender Equity Theme, Effective Gender Mainstreaming or Some Gender Elements under ADBs Guidelines for Gender Mainstreaming Categories of ADB Projects. Projects under these categories incorporate gender equality in their project design. CEFPFs percentage exceeds ADBs target of having at least 75% of committed operations promote gender equality by 2030 as outlined in ADBs Strategy 2030.
- In 2024, 59% of CEFPF-supported projects will provide health and productivity co-benefits from the increased use of clean energy. On average, 52% of CEFPF-supported projects have health and productivity targets in their project designs. Specific to productivity, a total of 6,881 jobs have been created by projects supported by CEFPF, of which 307 jobs are held by women. The Embassy will engage in dialogue with ADB at the next annual meeting to encourage an increase in employment opportunities for women.
